rationale: METeOR's PBS DSS maps this element to "Variable name = DRG_TYP_CD", its short name is "Type of drug prescribed (broad category)" against the PLIDA description "Type of drug supplied - broad category code", and it publishes a closed 21-code XX domain.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: CA Highly Specialised Drugs (community access items) CT Chemotherapy support drugs
supersedes_rationale: The generator currently fills DRG_TYP_CD from the `benefit_type` column of inst/extdata/pbs_item_lookup.csv, which is the PBS Schedule's benefit_type_code (A/R/S/U = authority required / restricted / streamlined / unrestricted). That is the restriction level of a listing, a different concept from the claim's broad drug category. The four generated values are not members of this domain.

rationale: The METeOR page carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = PHRMCY_APPRVL_TYP_CD", and its guide for use ties code 0 to section 90, code D to section 92 and code H to section 94 of the National Health Act 1953, which is the statutory structure the assignment expected.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: Y Participating public hospital B Non-participating public hospital 0 Approved community pharmacy
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass recorded "public code table not found". The generator's A/F pair (A for a plain approved pharmacy, F for friendly society) has the friendly-society code right but the ordinary community-pharmacy code wrong: the published code is the digit 0, not A, and there is no A in the domain.

value_source: AIHW METeOR 603862, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber type, code A (Department of Health)
rationale: The METeOR page carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = PRSCRBR_TYP_CD" and publishes the closed single-character domain, including the historical code B for prescribers qualified as both medical and dental practitioners.
evidence_quote: M Medical practitioner D Dental practitioner B Both O Optometrist N Nurse practitioner W Midwife
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass recorded "public code table not found". The generator's M/N pair is a correct subset of this domain but omits D, B, O and W. Code B should only appear before 2008, O only from 1 January 2008, and N and W only from 1 September 2010, per the METeOR guide for use - useful if the generator is made period-aware.

value_source: AIHW METeOR 600681, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—specialty of prescriber, group code NN (Department of Health)
rationale: METeOR 600681 is the only PBS specialty element that carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD", and its four groups map cleanly onto the generator's existing GP/SP/OT split; confidence is medium because METeOR also publishes a 66-code four-digit element, 607130 "Major specialty of prescriber" (https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/607130), whose short name is the PLIDA description word for word, so an implementer should decide between NN and NNNN before relabelling.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: 01 General practitioner (GP) 02 Specialist 03 Allied health professional 04 Dental practitioner
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass recorded "public code table not found". Note METeOR states 607130 "is not part of the 2013-14 data extract provided to the states and territories", which is why I take the two-digit group as the field's domain despite the description matching the four-digit element's title.

values: 6 spaces: Not applicable, i.e. ineligible for Closing the Gap co-payment relief
CTGnnA: six-character annotation - literal 'CTG', a two-digit sequence number incremented within the prescriber's practice, then an alphabetic check digit
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603679, Patient—Closing the Gap co-payment eligibility indicator, code AAA[NNA] (Department of Health)
rationale: The METeOR page carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = CTG_CD" and its short name is the PLIDA description verbatim; the domain is a structured six-character annotation code rather than an enumerated list, with blank meaning ineligible.
evidence_quote: The first three characters of the code should be 'CTG', followed by a two-digit number
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass inferred a Y/N flag and the generator emits Y/N. The published domain is format AAA[NNA], maximum six characters, with six spaces as the only supplementary value. A Y/N flag carries the same information but is not the published representation; a faithful column would be blank or a CTGnnX string. The check digit depends on the prescription date, so a generator can produce well-formed but not check-digit-valid codes.

value_source: PBS Schedule, Streamlined Authority item listing (Department of Health and Aged Care), with the format stated in PBS Explanatory Notes section 1.2
rationale: The PBS publishes a streamlined authority code against each restriction on each Authority required (STREAMLINED) item; I scraped the A-Z browse listing (23 pages, 4,468 item/brand rows) and found 1,031 distinct codes, all bare 4- or 5-digit numerics, which matches the Explanatory Notes' "four or five digit streamlined authority code".
evidence_quote: the authority prescription form must include a four or five digit streamlined authority code
supersedes_rationale: The generator currently writes S0001-S9999, an invented alphabetic-prefixed form, and only when the item lookup's benefit_type is S. The prefix is wrong: real codes are bare numerics such as 4512, 5942 and 14604. The 1,031 count is the current schedule only, so it is a floor, not the historical universe for 2006-2025; codes are also per-restriction, so one item can carry several (the listing shows cells like "4512-4454").

value_source: Australian Government Department of Health and Aged Care, Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits
rationale: The bundled inst/extdata/pbs_item_lookup.csv already serves as the domain: 4,274 real General Schedule item codes taken from the PBS public data API, and every code matches METeOR's published format NN[NNN]A with a final alphabetic check digit.
evidence_quote: Classification scheme: Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits ... Format: NN[NNN]A
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass called this inferred. It is not: the generator samples from a real published item list. The one caveat worth recording is vintage - the lookup is a single current-schedule snapshot (program_code GE, non-effective items dropped), so items delisted before 2026 never appear even in 2006-2015 tables, and the five-digit codes introduced from December 2013 appear in earlier years where they did not yet exist.

values: 1-98: number of repeat supplies authorised by the prescriber
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603919, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised prescription repeats, total number N[N] (Department of Health)
rationale: Open count, not a code list, but METeOR does publish the representation for this exact variable name: format N[N], 0 for single-supply prescriptions, and the supplementary value 99 for not stated.
supersedes_rationale: The existing "not specified" treatment is fine and the generator's 0-15 range sits inside the published format; the only additions are the two-digit width cap and the reserved 99.

values: 2-98: number of times previously supplied, including the original supply
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603916, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of times previously supplied, total number N[N] (Department of Health)
rationale: Open count, but METeOR publishes the representation for this exact variable name: format N[N], counted inclusive of the original supply, with 99 reserved for not stated.
evidence_quote: For a 'single supply' prescription, this data item should have a value of 1
supersedes_rationale: The existing "not specified" treatment is defensible, but the generator's floor of 0 conflicts with the published guide for use, which says the count includes the original supply and so should be at least 1. Shifting the generated range from 0-6 to 1-7 would match the source at no cost.

value_domain: Short code distinguishing types of under co-payment prescription; null where the claim is not under co-payment (inferred)
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603902, PBS claim type, code A (supports the under co-payment concept and its collection from 1 April 2012, not this field's code list)
rationale: No published code table found: this variable is absent from METeOR's PBS data set specification, which covers every other coded field in this assignment under its exact PLIDA variable name, and the PBS under co-payment statistics pages publish no type classification. The generator's existing 1/2 split on patient category, null when the claim is above co-payment, is a defensible shape given the field only exists on under co-payment claims, so I recommend leaving it alone and simply labelling it guessed.
